title: An indexed file with an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY that allows duplicates
shapes: AIXA AIXAKSD: SELECT ORD-FILE ... RECORD KEY IS ORD-ID / ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS ORD-CUST WITH DUPLICATES
asserts: The SELECT is one file_control fact (select ORD-FILE, assign ORDKSD, organization INDEXED, access_mode DYNAMIC, record_key ORD-ID) carrying alternate_keys [{name ORD-CUST, duplicates true}]. ORD-CUST is not the record_key: the prime key stays ORD-ID. Without the DUPLICATES phrase the alternate key values would have to be unique, so the flag is part of the fact, not decoration.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified, the values contained in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY data item must be unique among records in the file.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If the DUPLICATES phrase is specified, the values contained in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY data item can be duplicated within any records in the file.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: In sequential access, the records with duplicate keys are retrieved in the order in which they were placed in the file. In random access, only the first record written in a series of records with duplicate keys can be retrieved.
